meta.title: Back Up Chrome Bookmarks | Snug
meta.description: Back up Chrome bookmarks by exporting an HTML file by hand, or schedule exports with Snug's Auto-export. Menu paths verified {date}.

title: How do I back up my Chrome bookmarks?
directAnswer: In Chrome, open {fromExportPath} and save the file, which Chrome names {fromExportFile}. To repeat that on a schedule, turn on Snug's Auto-export, which saves exports to Downloads or a folder you choose.

builtIn.title: The built-in way
builtIn.intro: Chrome exports your bookmarks to an HTML file. Do it by hand whenever you want a fresh copy.
steps: Save the file. Chrome names it {fromExportFile}.
Copy the file to a second place, such as a USB drive. A backup that lives only on this computer is lost with it.
To check the backup, open the file in a text editor or drag it into a browser tab. It lists your folders and bookmarks.

carriesOver.title: The profile file and what the export holds
carriesOver.intro: Chrome also keeps your bookmarks in a file called {fromProfileFile} inside the profile folder. Close Chrome before you copy it as a raw backup.
items: The profile folder is often named Default. Other profiles use other folder names.
Kept in the HTML file, per {fromName}: {fromHtmlKeeps}.
Left out of the HTML file, per {fromName}: {fromHtmlDrops}.

withSnug.title: With Snug's Auto-export
withSnug.intro: Snug runs in Chrome. Auto-export saves your bookmarks to files on this computer on a schedule. It does not upload them anywhere and does not sync them between browsers or devices.
steps: Install Snug in Chrome and open its Auto-export page.
Turn on Enable Auto-export and choose one or more of the six formats. HTML is one of them.
Choose how often it runs: hourly, every 12 hours, daily, every 3 days or weekly. Daily, every-3-days and weekly runs happen at a preferred time, and weekly runs also let you pick the day.
Under Save to, choose Downloads, or choose Custom folder and select Choose folder… to pick any folder on your computer.
Set Keep the last N runs. The default is 10, and 0 keeps everything. After each successful run, Snug deletes only the files of its own older runs.
Click Export now to test the setup. It exports with the settings on screen and does not change your schedule.
withSnug.snapshot: Files are saved without a save dialog. If a file with the same name exists, Snug adds a (1) suffix and never overwrites it. After a browser restart, Chrome asks once to confirm access to a Custom folder: choose "Allow on every visit". If the browser was closed when a run was due, Snug catches up shortly after the next start.

goesWrong.title: If something goes wrong
items: No files appear. Open the Auto-export page: the status card shows the last run and its outcome, with the error message when it failed.
The page shows Folder access needed. Click Allow access. Until you do, runs fail and nothing is saved to Downloads instead.
Older backups disappeared. Retention deletes only files Snug itself saved, beyond the number you set to keep. Set it to 0 to keep everything.
You expected a copy on another device. Auto-export writes files on this computer only. Copy the folder to another disk or device yourself.

verified: Menu paths, file names and profile folders were read from {fromName}'s help pages and Chromium's own documents on {date}. Browser menus change between versions, so check the source if a path differs on your screen. Snug's behavior comes from its Auto-export guide.
